title: Enroll a router in a PKI
blurb: Generate keys, trust a CA and enroll R1 for a certificate with SCEP, ready for certificate-based VPNs.
scenario: Pre-shared keys don't scale to dozens of branch VPNs. The company runs a certificate authority with **SCEP** at **http://10.10.99.40:80**. Enroll R1 so it can authenticate VPN peers with certificates.
topology:
R1 ── SCEP ── CA 10.10.99.40
      RSA key pair: R1-KEY
objectives: Tell symmetric and asymmetric cryptography apart
Generate a key pair and define a trustpoint

steps.title: Which cryptography does what?
steps.learn: **Symmetric** algorithms (AES) use one shared key and are fast, so they encrypt bulk data. **Asymmetric** algorithms (RSA, ECDSA) use a key pair and are slow, so they're used for signatures and key exchange. **Hashes** (SHA-256) prove integrity.
steps.task: Match each job to the algorithm type used for it.

fields.label: Encrypting the data in an IPsec tunnel
Detecting that a file was changed

steps.title: Keys and trustpoint
steps.learn: A **trustpoint** describes one CA: how to reach it, which key pair to use, what to put in the certificate request, and how to check revocation.
steps.task: Generate general-purpose RSA keys labeled **R1-KEY**, **2048** bits. Create trustpoint **CA-TP**: enrollment URL **http://10.10.99.40:80**, subject name **CN=R1.scor.lab**, key pair **R1-KEY**, revocation check **crl**.
steps.hint: `crypto key generate rsa general-keys label R1-KEY modulus 2048`, then `crypto pki trustpoint CA-TP`, `enrollment url http://10.10.99.40:80`, `subject-name CN=R1.scor.lab`, `rsakeypair R1-KEY`, `revocation-check crl`.

steps.title: Trust the CA, then enroll
steps.learn: First, **authenticate** the CA: download its certificate and confirm the fingerprint out of band. Then **enroll**: send a signed certificate request and receive R1's identity certificate.
steps.task: Authenticate trustpoint **CA-TP**, then enroll in it.
steps.hint: `crypto pki authenticate CA-TP`, then `crypto pki enroll CA-TP`. Both are global configuration commands.

steps.title: Revocation
steps.question: A branch router is stolen. How do the other routers stop trusting its certificate?

options.text: The CA revokes the certificate, and peers that check the CRL (or ask an OCSP responder) reject it.
Delete the CA certificate from every router.
options.why: That would break trust in every certificate the CA issued, not just the stolen one.

options.text: Nothing is needed, because certificates expire in a few minutes.
options.why: Identity certificates usually last a year or more. Revocation covers the time before expiry.

summary: An RSA key pair, a trustpoint pointing at the SCEP CA with a subject name and CRL checking, CA authentication with fingerprint checking, enrollment, and verification of the identity and CA certificates.
